argument_summary: The strongest admissible position is not that rollout controls alone made certification compliant. The admissible record supports a narrower claim: certification is supportable only as a caveated, monitored launch because aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and staged 8% rollout plus rollback are legitimate risk-management controls, while the fraud dispute review weakness remains unresolved and exposed. On this record, the decision can be defended only if the audit packet treats the limitation as an expressly disclosed residual risk rather than as a cured issue.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the auditor narrows the treatment to caveated compliance rather than treating the packet as an unsupported clean-certification claim. That preserves the locked certification posture without overstating what the evidence proves. The business value of that approach is that it avoids unnecessary disruption to the staged rollout while aligning the packet with the actual evidentiary limits.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against any broad defense based only on rollout controls. The admissible policy text says disclosure is still required when a named launch use case has a material unresolved limitation and remains exposed, unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible rollout evidence shows the affected fraud dispute review segment remains exposed, and the admissible risk-acceptance evidence shows the draft is unsigned and does not cover that exposure. So the policy-consistent defense is caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure and residual-risk acknowledgment, not clean compliance based on monitoring and rollback alone.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the model-card or launch materials actually contain the required explicit disclosure.
The current admissible record does not contain an approved risk acceptance covering continued exposure of the fraud dispute review segment.
Rollout controls, 8% launch, monitoring, and rollback are insufficient by themselves under the stated policy while the affected segment remains exposed.
A clean compliance finding would overstate what the present evidence supports.
